title: Perfect-complex duality on a small ringed site
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the chosen module universe [def-weil-size-convention], with $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings and $D(\mathcal O)$ the unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $P\in D(\mathcal O)$ be perfect: locally on the site it is represented by a bounded cochain complex whose terms are direct summands of finite free $\mathcal O$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Use K-flat relative derived tensor [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then $P^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(P,\mathcal O)$ is perfect, the canonical bidual map $P\to(P^\vee)^\vee$ is an isomorphism, and for every $N\in D(\mathcal O)$ the canonical evaluation comparison is a natural isomorphism
$$P^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}N\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(P,N).$$

source.place: Tag 08JJ, label lemma-dual-perfect-complex; symmetry interchanges the tensor factors in the displayed isomorphism.

proof.text: Choose a normalized closed tensor-Hom model M using [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps]. On each slice choose a normalized model and the exact restriction functor F together with its tensor, Hom, unit, bidual and evaluation comparisons. The termwise comparison is naturally isomorphic to ordinary slice restriction by identity module morphisms.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, local strictly perfect calculation and descent; Tag 08FI for restriction of K-injectives.

proof.text: The literal perfectness definition [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package] is equivalent to local existence of bounded finite-free-retract models E and derived isomorphisms F(P) isomorphic to Q(E). One direction localizes the given quasi-isomorphisms. Conversely choose a single global K-injective resolution of P. Exact extension by zero is left adjoint to slice restriction, so restriction preserves K-injectives. A derived map from Q(E) into that restricted K-injective is represented by an actual chain map; invertibility after Q makes it a quasi-isomorphism. This gives the actual maps required in the perfectness definition.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, local strictly perfect calculation and descent; Tag 08FI for restriction of K-injectives.

proof.text: The family of all objects admitting one of these local models covers the site: the covering sieve supplied for any V is contained in its generated sieve. These restrictions jointly detect isomorphisms in the derived category. Represent a morphism by an actual chain map from a representative of its source into a K-injective representative of its target. If all restrictions are invertible, every restricted chain map is a quasi-isomorphism. Exact restriction commutes with homology, and the sheaf-cover criterion [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism] shows its global homology maps are invertible. Hence the original chain map is a quasi-isomorphism and the derived morphism is invertible.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, local strictly perfect calculation and descent; Tag 08FI for restriction of K-injectives.

proof.text: For a bounded finite-free-retract complex E on a slice, [lem-sfb-ringed-site-strict-perfect-hom] gives the actual ordinary dual D, its bounded finite-free package, the required ordinary-to-derived Hom comparisons, and invertibility of the actual ordinary bidual and evaluation chain maps. The dual is K-flat: finite powers of the tensor unit are dualizable by induction with biproducts; dualizability passes to retracts and implies flatness. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] to the bounded dual. The normalized bidual equation [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps] then shows biduality is invertible for Q(E). For arbitrary N choose a K-flat resolution [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; the normalized tensor-Hom equation and the ordinary evaluation isomorphism show evaluation for Q(E),N is invertible. Transport through the chosen isomorphism of the K-flat resolution with N.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, local strictly perfect calculation and descent; Tag 08FI for restriction of K-injectives.

proof.text: On each chosen slice, the Hom comparison for F and the unit comparison identify the restricted derived dual of P with Q(D), where D is the bounded finite-free-retract ordinary dual of its local model E. The equivalence of step 2 therefore proves that the global derived dual of P is perfect.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, local strictly perfect calculation and descent; Tag 08FI for restriction of K-injectives.

proof.text: Naturality of the canonical bidual transports its invertibility through the local isomorphism F(P) isomorphic to Q(E). The bidual restriction equation has only isomorphisms as comparison factors. Cancel them and apply joint detection from step 3 to prove the global canonical bidual is invertible.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, local strictly perfect calculation and descent; Tag 08FI for restriction of K-injectives.

proof.text: Use source naturality of evaluation to transport step 4 through each local model. The evaluation restriction equation has invertible tensor and Hom comparison factors, so cancellation and step 3 imply that each global evaluation component is invertible. Finally the left-order evaluation is the braiding followed by that component. It is invertible, and the componentwise criterion for a natural transformation proves the last assertion.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, local strictly perfect calculation and descent; Tag 08FI for restriction of K-injectives.
